title: Rajkumar Hirani Finally Made Something for Your Phone — and He Brought the Munna Bhai Gang
excerpt: The man behind 3 Idiots and PK launches his son, reunites with Arshad Warsi, and takes on cybercrime in Goa. Pritam and Pedro starts streaming today on JioHotstar.
body:
There is a particular kind of filmmaker who makes you wait. Rajkumar Hirani is that filmmaker. Five movies in two decades — **Munna Bhai M.B.B.S.**, **Lage Raho Munna Bhai**, **3 Idiots**, **PK**, **Sanju** — and every single one became a cultural event. He doesn't do small. He doesn't do quiet. And he has never, until today, made anything for a screen smaller than a cinema.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=uCjkRVV0-qU</youtube>

**Pritam and Pedro**, which starts streaming on JioHotstar on July 3, is Hirani's long-awaited streaming debut. And it is, in every way, a family affair.

His son **Vir Hirani** makes his acting debut as Pritam Parker, a tech-savvy young man with a talent for hacking and a tendency to find himself in situations he can't code his way out of. Opposite him is **Arshad Warsi** — the man who made Circuit immortal — as Inspector Pedro Gonsalves, an old-school Goan cop who trusts gut instinct over gadgets and has just been transferred to the cyber cell as punishment.

> "I think Raju has a little faith in me as an actor. He gives me various things to do. And I like it, I enjoy it. I am waiting for some more to come." — Arshad Warsi

The pairing is classic Hirani: two people who should not work together, forced to work together, eventually discovering they need each other. Pedro's world is danda and interrogation rooms. Pritam's is data and dark web rabbit holes. When a kidnapping case collides with a cybercrime ring in the sun-drenched chaos of Goa, the odd couple dynamic goes from comic to urgent.

The supporting cast reads like a greatest-hits reel. **Vikrant Massey** plays Martin, the antagonist — a significant pivot for an actor who's spent the last few years as Bollywood's most sympathetic everyman. **Boman Irani** and **Mona Singh** hold down pivotal roles. And then there's the open secret that **Sanjay Dutt** has a cameo — a detail Warsi let slip at the trailer launch with characteristic nonchalance, essentially confirming a mini Munna Bhai reunion before the publicists could stop him.


The show was born during the COVID-19 lockdown, when the Mumbai Cyber Cell approached Hirani about making a film on cybercrime. He met writer Amit Dubey, and the idea crystallised into something more playful than a procedural — a buddy comedy wrapped in a thriller, set against the beaches and back alleys of Goa. Hirani wrote the series with **Abhijat Joshi** (his longtime collaborator on 3 Idiots and PK) and Suyash Trivedi, then handed the directing chair to **Avinash Arun**, the cinematographer behind Sacred Games and the critically adored Marathi film Killa. Hirani produced and edited — his fingerprints are on every frame.

The makers describe it as a world "where data meets danda, chaos meets confusion." Based on the trailer, that's exactly what it delivers: rapid-fire comedy, mismatched energy, and enough cybercrime intrigue to keep you scrolling past the opening credits.

## What Diaspora Viewers Need to Know

Pritam and Pedro streams exclusively on **JioHotstar** starting July 3, 2026. JioHotstar is available internationally and offers Hindi-language streaming with subtitles. If you have an active subscription, you're set. If you don't — this might be the one that gets you to sign up.

The series has **8 episodes** in its first season. Music is by **Shantanu Moitra** (songs) and **Sanjay Wandrekar** (score).

## Why This Matters

Hirani stepping into streaming isn't just a format shift — it's a signal. The man who built a career on theatrical tentpoles has acknowledged what everyone in Mumbai has known for years: the living room is the new single screen. When the architect of India's most beloved comedies decides to build for your phone, the platform wins before a single frame plays.

But the real story here might be Vir Hirani. Star kids enter the industry every month, and most of them vanish just as quickly. What makes this debut different is the pedigree of the storyteller behind it. Rajkumar Hirani doesn't gamble on screen presence — he builds it. He turned Sanjay Dutt into a lovable gangster. He made Aamir Khan a credible alien. If anyone can sculpt a debut that sticks, it's him.

Pritam and Pedro is the kind of show you'll either binge in a weekend or fight about in the family group chat. Either way, Hirani's finally in your living room.
